hook.text: A virus that kills cancer — oncolytic viruses infect tumor cells and burst them open while sparing healthy tissue.

buildup.text: Viruses are engineered to replicate only inside cancer cells — mutations disable their growth in normal tissue.

discovery.text: T-VEC is an approved herpes virus that destroys melanoma — it also releases signals that recruit the immune system.

twist.text: The immune system often clears the virus before it reaches distant tumors — delivery remains a major barrier.

climax.text: Combining oncolytic viruses with checkpoint inhibitors boosts response rates — the virus primes what immunotherapy finishes.

punchline.text: Fight fire with fire — oncolytic viruses turn infections into cancer cures.

quiz.question: How does T-VEC treat melanoma?
options: It blocks blood supply to melanoma tumors
It is an engineered herpes virus that selectively infects and destroys melanoma cells while stimulating immune response
It delivers chemotherapy drugs directly inside cancer cells
